question: According to the manual, what is true of a vehicle that has components marked or labeled?
choice_a: The components are noted but testing proceeds normally
choice_b: The vehicle cannot be used for the Vehicle Inspection test
choice_c: The driver must replace them before testing begins
choice_d: The examiner will overlook those components
explanation: The manual states, "Any vehicle that has components marked or labeled cannot be used for the Vehicle Inspection test."
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-1

question: When should the engine oil level be checked, and where must the level be?
choice_a: Checked with engine running; must be below the refill mark
choice_b: Checked with engine off; must be at the full mark
choice_c: Checked with engine running; must be at the add mark
choice_d: Checked with engine off; must be above the refill mark
explanation: The manual says to check oil level when the engine is off and that the level must be above the refill mark.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-1

question: When inspecting engine compartment belts for snugness, how much play should there be at the center of the belt?
explanation: The manual specifies checking belts for snugness of "1/2 to 3/4 inch play at center of belt" along with cracks, frays, loose fibers, or wear.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-1

question: During the Safe Start procedure, what should the driver do with the clutch after starting the engine?
choice_a: Keep the clutch depressed until the engine reaches idling speed, then release slowly
choice_b: Keep the clutch depressed only for five seconds after starting
choice_c: Release the clutch immediately after the engine starts
choice_d: Release the clutch before starting the engine
explanation: The manual describes the Safe Start procedure as starting the vehicle and keeping the clutch depressed until the engine reaches idling speed, then releasing the clutch slowly.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-1

question: The air compressor should build air pressure to governor cut-out at approximately what psi range?
explanation: The manual states the air compressor builds air pressure to governor cut-out at approximately 120-140 psi or as specified by the manufacturer.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-2

question: Besides spare electrical fuses and a fire extinguisher, what emergency equipment must be checked according to the manual?
choice_a: One reflective triangle and a first aid kit
choice_b: Three red reflective triangles and 6 fusees or 3 liquid burning flares
choice_c: Four fusees and a tow strap
choice_d: Two red reflective triangles and 4 fusees
explanation: The manual lists checking for three red reflective triangles and 6 fusees or 3 liquid burning flares, plus a properly charged and securely mounted fire extinguisher.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-2

question: According to the manual, what colors should clearance lights be?
explanation: The manual specifies clearance lights should be "red on rear, amber elsewhere" as part of verifying correct color for lights and reflectors.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-2

question: Which of the following is NOT among the dash indicators listed for testing during the cab check?
explanation: The manual lists left turn signal, right turn signal, four-way emergency flashers, high beam headlight, and ABS indicator as dash indicators to test; a fuel gauge is not listed among them.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-2

question: How must checks of brake, turn signal, and four-way flasher functions be performed, per the manual?
choice_d: Only if the examiner requests it
explanation: The manual notes: "Checks of brake, turn signal and four-way flasher functions must be done separately."
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-3

question: What happens if a driver fails to perform both components of the hydraulic brake check?
choice_a: Nothing; it is an optional check
choice_b: It results in an automatic failure of the vehicle inspection test
choice_c: A written warning is issued but testing continues
choice_d: The driver may retake just that portion
explanation: The manual states, "Failure to perform both components of the hydraulic brake check will result in an automatic failure of the vehicle inspection test."
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-3

question: In the hydraulic brake check, after pumping the brake pedal three times, how long should it be held down while checking it does not move?
explanation: The manual instructs to "Pump the brake pedal three times, then hold it down for five seconds. The brake pedal should not move (depress) during the five seconds."
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-3

topic: Air Brake Static Pressure Loss - Single Vehicle
question: During the air brake check, with the foot brake fully applied and held for one minute, how much can the air pressure drop for a single (non-combination) vehicle?
explanation: The manual states to check that air pressure does not drop more than three pounds in one minute for a single vehicle (four pounds for a combination vehicle).
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-3

topic: Air Brake Static Pressure Loss - Combination Vehicle
question: During the same static air pressure check, how much can the pressure drop in one minute for a combination vehicle?
explanation: The manual specifies the air pressure should not drop more than four pounds in one minute for a combination vehicle (three pounds for a single vehicle).
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-3

question: According to the manual, low air warning devices should activate before air pressure drops below what level?
explanation: The manual states low air warning devices (buzzer, light, flag) should activate before air pressure drops below 55 psi or the level specified by the manufacturer.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-3

question: On a tractor-trailer combination vehicle, at what psi range should the tractor protection valve and parking brake valve close (pop out) during the air brake check?
explanation: The manual states that at a range between 20-45 psi (or as specified by the manufacturer), the tractor protection valve and parking brake valve should close (pop out).
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-3

question: During the service brake check, at what speed should the driver pull forward before applying the service brake and stopping?
explanation: The manual instructs: "Pull forward at 5 mph, apply the service brake and stop."
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-3

topic: Wheel Chocks During Air Brake Check
question: According to the manual, when should wheel chocks be used during the air brake check?
choice_c: In areas where an incline is present, for safety purposes
explanation: The manual states, "For safety purposes, in areas where an incline is present, you will use wheel chocks during the air brake check."
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-3

question: For manual slack adjustors, how far should the brake pushrod move when pulled by hand with the brakes released?
choice_a: It should not move at all
choice_d: Not more than half an inch
explanation: The manual states that for manual slack adjustors, the brake pushrod should not move more than one inch (with the brakes released) when pulled by hand.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-4

question: What is the minimum tread depth for steering axle tires, according to the manual?
explanation: The manual specifies a minimum tread depth of 4/32 inch on steering axle tires (2/32 inch on all other tires).
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-5

topic: Class A vs Class B/C Test Versions
question: How many versions of the Vehicle Inspection test exist for Class A CDL applicants, compared to Class B and C applicants?
choice_a: Both Class A and Class B/C have three versions
choice_b: Class A has three versions; Class B/C has four
choice_c: Both Class A and Class B/C have four versions
choice_d: Class A has four versions; Class B/C has three
explanation: The manual states Class A applicants perform one of four versions of the Vehicle Inspection, while Class B applicants perform one of three versions.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-9
